opaque_id.provenance: Declared task index via separate task path
opaque_id.world_a_definition: first_occurrence: z^*_A(x, k) = min { i | x_i == y_k }
opaque_id.world_b_definition: last_occurrence: z^*_B(x, k) = max { i | x_i == y_k }
opaque_id.training_history_identity: On all clean instances x in X_clean, |{i | x_i == y_k}| <= 1, so min == max. Clean token targets, cross-entropy losses, and gradients are bitwise identical. Under duplicate-masked training, duplicate cells receive zero gradient.
opaque_id.test_collision_divergence: On test input x_test = [A, B, C, D, A] with y_0 = A, z^*_A = 0 != 4 = z^*_B. Learner parameters are identical, coordinate accuracy is bounded by 0.5 < 0.95 floor.

compositional_semantic_descriptor.formal_definition: O_task = D = (OpFamily, ArgSlots, Schema) in D_comp
compositional_semantic_descriptor.provenance: Pre-declared structured AST / schema provided model-visible at inference time
compositional_semantic_descriptor.charter_boundary_constraint: Per Phase C Charter and AGENTS.md, D cannot contain hard-coded correct routing map tables z^*(k) and must not bypass primitive execution through decoder.
compositional_semantic_descriptor.world_a_definition: Satisfies D with first-occurrence tie-breaking rule z^*_A(x, k) = min { i | x_i == y_k }
compositional_semantic_descriptor.world_b_definition: Satisfies D with last-occurrence tie-breaking rule z^*_B(x, k) = max { i | x_i == y_k }
compositional_semantic_descriptor.training_history_identity: Both worlds fully and truthfully satisfy descriptor D. On all clean training instances, outputs, losses, and gradients are identical.
compositional_semantic_descriptor.test_collision_divergence: On collision sequence x_test = [A, B, C, D, A] with y_0 = A, z^*_A = 0 != 4 = z^*_B. Model observing identical D cannot distinguish coordinates.

finite_output_labeled_support_set.provenance: In-context demonstrations or few-shot support batch via separate task path
finite_output_labeled_support_set.charter_boundary_constraint: Support set contains token labels y in V, never oracle routing coordinates z in {0, ..., L-1}.
finite_output_labeled_support_set.world_a_definition: z^*_A(x, k) = min { i | x_i == y_k }, f_A(x)_k = x_{z^*_A(x, k)}
finite_output_labeled_support_set.world_b_definition: z^*_B(x, k) = max { i | x_i == y_k }, f_B(x)_k = x_{z^*_B(x, k)}
finite_output_labeled_support_set.universal_token_identity_theorem: For all x in V^L and all k, x_{min {i | x_i == y_k}} == y_k == x_{max {i | x_i == y_k}}. Hence f_A(x) == f_B(x) identically across all sequences.
finite_output_labeled_support_set.support_set_observation_identity: For any support set S = {(x^(m), y^(m))}, y_A^(m) == y_B^(m) for all m in {1, ..., K}. Observed support set is bitwise identical in World A and World B.
finite_output_labeled_support_set.training_history_identity: All training inputs, targets, CE losses, and gradients are bitwise identical across all training steps.
finite_output_labeled_support_set.test_collision_divergence: On test input x_test = [A, B, C, D, A] with y_0 = A, z^*_A = 0 != 4 = z^*_B. Model observing identical support set S and identical training history cannot break symmetry.

bounded_separating_support_set_audit.audit_question: Can an oracle-free pre-fixed bounded separating support set uniquely identify a finite relation hypothesis class to resolve routing ambiguity?

extensional_separation_feasibility.condition: If hypothesis class H_rel = {R_1, ..., R_M} consists of relations with distinct extensional mappings f_i != f_j, a bounded support set S_sep = {x_ij} of size at most M(M-1)/2 distinguishes which extensional mapping f is active.

failure_mechanisms.mechanism: Intra-relation coordinate ambiguity under identical extensional mapping
failure_mechanisms.detail: World A (min occurrence) and World B (max occurrence) have f_A == f_B on all inputs. No token-labeled support set can ever separate them because output tokens are identical.

Restricting H_rel to exclude alternative routing rules requires hard-coding a canonical routing map z^* into the hypothesis definition, violating the non-negotiable rule that task-side identifiers cannot become hard-coded correct routing maps.
Phase C Charter and G1 require transfer to unseen open-world relation components. An open-world hypothesis class is unbounded, making a pre-fixed bounded separating support set impossible.

bounded_separating_support_set_audit.verdict: FAIL (Separating support set resolves extensional function identity, but fails to identify semantic routing coordinates on collision cells without hard-coded oracle priors).

adr_0151_scope_resolution.rationale: Counterexamples hold across all three canonical task-side observable classifications (opaque ID, compositional descriptor, and finite output-labeled support set). ADR-0151's stoppage rationale is not limited to Contract-v1, but represents a quantifier-complete impossibility theorem for H-C1 under all permitted oracle-free observables.
